hub-multiple-sclerosis:
# Multiple sclerosis

An immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. The
hub collects what this base knows about mechanism, risk and treatment.

- [[concept-demyelination]] is the shared lesion mechanism.
- [[concept-relapsing-remitting-course]] is the commonest presentation.
- Risk carries a strong [[entity-hla-drb1-1501]] signal on top of
  [[entity-epstein-barr-virus]] exposure.

## Treatment

B-cell depletion ([[entity-ocrelizumab]]) and integrin blockade
([[entity-natalizumab]]) are the two best-evidenced disease-modifying routes
in this base.
concept-demyelination:
# Demyelination

Loss of the myelin sheath around axons, slowing or blocking conduction.
Repeated demyelination and incomplete remyelination underlie the accumulating
disability seen in [[concept-relapsing-remitting-course]].
entity-epstein-barr-virus:
# Epstein Barr virus

Near-universal exposure, but seroconversion precedes MS onset in longitudinal
military-cohort data ([[source-bjornevik-2022]]). Not sufficient on its own —
the risk is conditional on [[entity-hla-drb1-1501]].
source-bjornevik-2022:
# Longitudinal analysis reveals high prevalence of Epstein-Barr virus associated with multiple sclerosis

**Credibility:** peer reviewed · Science, 2022

A 10-million-person US military cohort. MS risk increased 32-fold after EBV
seroconversion and was not increased after infection with other viruses.
